title: Stop refuses to end a turn with an open CI run and no check-in set
why: CI waits have no enforcer: a session can end its turn on an open run with no check-in, and nothing wakes it. OWNER ITEMS 11:52 CST Nov 14 (lane ci-wait-stop-checkin-v2, draft #3410 which replaces #3063; message 11:43 CST; triage read none of its code): two questions are on the waiting page. Item 836 (pick-ci-wait-one-wait): the hook keeps one wait, the newest ready call; ready PR 5, ready PR 6, then a green line that names no PR closes the wait and PR 5 has no check-in while Stop passes (hooks/stall_watch.py open_ci_wait; reviewer round 1 probe). Option a keep one wait (starred at the lane's recommendation), b one wait per ready PR. Item 837 (pick-ci-wait-checkin-tools): the check counts CronCreate and any check-in covers the wait; test CI05 in hooks/test_stall_watch_stop.py pins it; the coordinator picked keep at 11:07 CST (undoable). Option a keep four tools (widens the check, not starred), b send_later only. Both are recorded Limits in decision ci-wait-reads-run-status; the lane does not wait. Owner ruling read by triage: own-ci-wait-subscribe-guard (subscribe or poll first; check-ins are the safety net), which names no tool and no wait count. DONE 14:39 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:42, REST 14:39; relayed; triage read no diff): #3063 (an undo or draft-again closes the CI wait; a branch-named wait closes on a merge of any PR) merged 14:38:37 CST as dff2cf430350d61b7c223af3e6725db40c4ba83d, alone on its green ready run 43635026510 (green 20:33:36Z). #3410 was closed as replaced earlier (archive/ci-wait-stop-checkin-v2). Owner items 836 (one wait or one per ready PR) and 837 (four check-in tools or send_later only) stay open.
